classification.difficultyReason: Isolate the squared radius in the supplied volume formula, take its positive square root, and convert centimetres to millimetres before rounding.

content.prompt: The volume, $V$ cm³, of a cylinder is given by $V=\pi r^2h$, where $r$ cm is the radius and $h$ cm is the height. Find the radius, correct to the nearest millimetre, of a cylinder with a volume of 100 cm³ and a height of 8 cm.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}V&=\pi r^2h\\r^2&=\frac{V}{\pi h}\\r&=\sqrt{\frac{V}{\pi h}}\\r&=\sqrt{\frac{100}{8\pi}}\text{ cm}\\r&=10\sqrt{\frac{100}{8\pi}}\text{ mm}\\r&\approx19.9471\text{ mm}\\r&\approx20\text{ mm}\quad\text{(nearest millimetre)}\end{align*}$$
Use the positive square root because the radius is positive.
